parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module passes. Both files deal with one concern: application-level failures and how they are classified in a transport-neutral way. ApplicationError.ts defines the application error types: an abstract ApplicationError base, plus ValidationError, NotFoundError and ConflictError. errorClassification.ts turns those errors, and the related domain errors, into a ClassifiedError with a kind and a code. The classifier relies on the module's own error classes through instanceof checks. It doesn't match on message strings or error names, so it doesn't bypass the abstractions. The error-to-kind/code mapping exists only in classifyError. Since the HTTP error handler imports classifyError instead of keeping its own mapping, the rule stays in one place. Each error class builds its own message, and no invariant is repeated. Classifying domain errors here is part of the same concern: it gives callers one place to describe any failure that reaches them. Import direction is out of scope for this review.
